budget.name: silicaflux-v-65
budget.source: DOCUMENTED: SilicaFlux-V reduced-ASIC p.1/p.3, 03-11-26 update p.7-9

rationale: 2484 of 2880 evaluated configurations fit the budget.
Best feasible suite geomean: 6.54 Gop/s (512KiB/16b/128w T16x16 V8 B16/F64 LPDDR2-800 x32, 7.8 mm2).
Recommended = smallest-area point within 90 % of that: 6.02 Gop/s in 4.6 mm2.
DMA path 1.97 GB/s vs DRAM sustained 2.08 GB/s.

findings.title: The SilicaFlux 2.5 tensor unit is starved by its own memory system.
findings.detail: In isolation it sustains 63.4 MAC/cycle (RTL_SIMULATION). It has no accumulation buffer, so every 4x4x4 product moves 32 B of operands in and 64 B of INT32 partials out; the tile's 16 B/cycle vector port and single 128-bit register write port cap it at 9 % of peak on a 512^3 GEMM even with MemoryFlow's DMA and DDR3 (2.40 of 25.3 Gop/s; bound: spm). The recommended outer-product array with in-array accumulators reaches 71.7 Gop/s (30x) in 4.6 mm^2.

findings.title: The SilicaFlux 2.x hierarchy above the tile exists only as instantiations.
findings.detail: silicaflux_top.sf (Gen-2.5) instantiates 27 module types; 26 of them (31 of 32 instances) are defined nowhere in the repository, including the L2 (sf_l2_cache, 2 MiB/complex), the LLC (sf_llc_bank, 8 x 4 MiB), the coherent crossbar, the memory fabric / AXI edge and the DMA bridge; the earlier silicaflux_rtl*.zip tops leave 10 of 11 types undefined. Only the Gen-1 top is complete. No SilicaFlux generation has a DRAM controller or PHY, so the external-memory side of the processor has to be designed, not integrated; MemoryFlow supplies the DMA, router, SPM, bridge and models for it.

findings.title: The Gen-2.5 compute tile cannot be elaborated from repository sources.
findings.detail: instance u_memory_controller of `memory_controller` (memory_controller.sf:94): 7/9 named ports and 2/2 parameters absent on the definition (e.g. req_valid_i, req_i, req_ready_o, rsp_valid_o). 29 of 30 package types used are defined by no package in set `sf25` (e.g. sf_alu_req_t, sf_alu_rsp_t, sf_br_mask_t, sf_br_res_t). The 2.5 testbenches tb_memory_controller.sf and tb_tensor_unit.sf also target interfaces the in-repo modules do not have. The individual units (memory_controller.sf, tensor_unit.sf, vector_engine.sf, register_bank.sf) do elaborate and were characterised directly.

findings.title: The documented SRAM area is about 3x optimistic.
findings.detail: The reduced-ASIC plan prices 256 KB at ~0.5 mm^2 using a 0.12 um^2 bitcell at 65 nm, about 4x smaller than published 65 nm high-density 6T cells (~0.52 um^2); with macro periphery MemoryFlow estimates 1.46 mm^2 at 65 nm and 6.89 mm^2 at 130 nm (ANALYTICAL, replace with memory-compiler data). At 130 nm the documented 256 KiB alone exceeds the 8 mm^2 core budget.

findings.title: The Gen-2.5 scratchpad controller is sound; its burst port is the weak link.
findings.detail: 150k+ self-checks pass on the unmodified memory_controller.sf (random traffic with backpressure, range/domain/overflow protection, parity detection, burst kill). Each port sustains ~1 request/cycle with a 3-cycle load latency; three requesters together move 29.9 B/cycle. The burst ('DMA') port allows one descriptor in flight with a done handshake, costing 3 (store) / 4 (load) cycles per burst: 0.20 beats/cycle at 1 beat, 0.80 at 16. A second descriptor slot would hide it.

findings.title: Gen-1 DFLOAD/DFSTORE bursts longer than 4 words are broken, and its SPM needs two write ports.
findings.detail: tb_sf1_memctrl: a DFSTORE of 8 words leaves 4 words unwritten and a DFLOAD of 8 re-reads words 0..3 (burst_addr never advances; the 128-bit buffer index wraps). The tile write-back port and the FSM write the array in the same cycle (2 writes measured), which no single-port SRAM macro can implement. Gen-1 bandwidth: 2.29 B/cycle per tile.

findings.title: DMA write acknowledgements, not reads, limit write-back to memory.
findings.detail: MemoryFlow sf_dma driving the unmodified 2.5 SPM through sf_mc25_vport_bridge: EXT->SPM 11.4 B/cycle, but SPM->EXT only 6.06 B/cycle: 8 outstanding write acks against a 20-cycle memory (Little's law: 8/21 x 16 B = 6.10). The models now carry this DMA write path (WOUT is an exploration dimension). SPM->SPM copies reach 8.0 B/cycle because reads and writes share the controller's single vector port.

findings.title: 130 nm is a fallback only if SilicaFlux-V shrinks to 128 KiB.
findings.detail: At 130 nm / 100 MHz no configuration with more than 128 KiB of SPM fits the 8 mm^2 core budget, and the best point reaches 1.28 Gop/s (vs 6.02 at 65 nm). DDR-class PHYs are not assumed at 130 nm; HyperRAM is the practical external memory there.

findings.title: For the full SilicaFlux, multi-channel LPDDR is the commercial sweet spot; HBM is a stretch option.
findings.detail: At 28 nm (no HBM PHY assumed) the recommended full chip is 32x 256KiB/4b/128w T16x16 V8 B16/F16 LPDDR4X-4266 2x32: 193 Gop/s suite geomean in 37 mm^2, 3.2 W; a single LPDDR4X x32 channel caps any configuration at 109 Gop/s. At 16 nm, LPDDR5 4x32 reaches 539 Gop/s (45 % of HBM2E's 1197) at 5.6 W vs 14.7 W, on an organic package instead of a 2.5D interposer. Tile scaling: 32 -> 64 tiles behind LPDDR4X-4266 2x32: +9 % performance for +83 % area (80 % of kernels bound by external memory or the DMA); 32 -> 64 tiles behind HBM2E 1 stack: +54 % performance for +45 % area (40 % of kernels bound by external memory or the DMA). Behind LPDDR the knee is well below the recommendation rule's pick (see the best-Gop/s-per-mm^2 rows); behind HBM more tiles keep paying. Full-chip envelopes are ASSUMPTIONS.

findings.title: A no-DRAM SilicaFlux-V demonstrates the core but starves the accelerators.
findings.detail: The documented no-DRAM target reaches 0.208 Gop/s suite geomean (QSPI-class link); the same machine with DDR3-1600 x16 reaches 1.55. On the 65 nm budget the best points per external memory are: QSPI 104 MHz (no DRAM) 0.25 Gop/s in 7.3 mm^2; HyperRAM 200 MHz x8 1.92 Gop/s in 5.5 mm^2; 2x HyperRAM 200 MHz x8 3.18 Gop/s in 5.5 mm^2; LPDDR2-800 x32 6.54 Gop/s in 7.8 mm^2; DDR3-1600 x16 6.54 Gop/s in 7.4 mm^2. HyperRAM (digital PHY, ~12 pins) is the low-cost, mature-node option; DDR3/LPDDR2 buys ~2-3x more.

findings.title: Outstanding DMA capacity must cover the external memory's bandwidth-delay product.
findings.detail: RTL reference (16 outstanding 64-bit beats, LPDDR2-800 x32, ~100 ns at 200 MHz): DMA read path 0.95 GB/s, write path 0.47 GB/s, DRAM sustained 2.08 GB/s. Covering the bandwidth-delay product of the recommended memory (DDR3-1600 x16) needs >= 13 128-bit beats in flight; the recommendation uses 16 outstanding reads and 32 outstanding write acks.

findings.title: A single shared DMA engine deadlocks against its own accelerator.
findings.detail: tb_system hung when an accelerator->SRAM (S2MM) channel occupied the only read engine while the operands it was waiting for were queued behind it. sf_dma now has independent MM2S/MEM2MEM and S2MM engines sharing one channel table; tb_dma, tb_system and tb_deadlock pass on the fixed RTL.

findings.title: Joined operand streams need FIFO depth >= DMA burst length (or sequenced loads).
findings.detail: tb_deadlock: with a 4-entry vector-unit FIFO and 16-beat bursts the DMA stalls after 4 beats and the watchdog fires; with 16 entries all 256 result beats complete. Predicate joined_stream_deadlock(4,16)=True.

findings.title: Bank-aligned SRAM-to-SRAM copies resonate into read/write bank conflicts.
findings.detail: RTL: a 4 KiB SPM->SPM copy with 16-beat bursts takes 652 cycles, but 556 cycles when the destination is skewed by one beat. XOR interleave or buffer skew removes it; the Python cycle model matches the skewed case but not the aligned resonance (listed as a model limitation).

findings.title: Power-of-two strides: XOR interleave fixes strides up to the fold width only.
findings.detail: RTL tb_spm (4 banks, 3 ports): stride 4 throughput 1.50 (modulo) -> 2.39 (XOR); stride 16 gives 1.00 with the 2-bit XOR fold. Block interleave is worst for streaming (1.23 at stride 1, 8 banks) and best for random traffic (2.63 requests/cycle).

findings.title: Accumulator double-buffering is worth ~1.8x on the tensor array when K equals the drain length.
findings.detail: RTL tb_accel, K=32: 88.6 % vs 49.7 % MAC utilisation. The analytical tile model (per tile max(K, drain) with double-buffering, K + drain without) reproduces RTL to 0.0 % after fitting its 1-3 cycle pipeline fill to these runs; the per-tile slope is not fitted.

findings.title: Response-credit depth must cover the 4-cycle SPM round trip.
findings.detail: RTL: RSP_DEPTH=2 gives 0.50 vs 1.00 requests/cycle single-port throughput with RSP_DEPTH=4, exactly as Little's law predicts (credits / round trip).

proposed.CPU cache interface: SilicaFlux core L1 <-> SPM host port adapter (SF-MEM valid/ready); MemoryFlow provides the TCM-style host port on sf_spm_banked port 2.
proposed.L2 / last-level cache: Not recommended for SilicaFlux-V first silicon: DMA-managed SPM gives deterministic bandwidth; revisit for multi-core variants.
proposed.Vector register file: Vector RF of the SilicaFlux vector pipeline (if separate from the streaming sf_vec_unit) -- 2R1W, 32 x VLEN, sf_sram_1r1w-based.
proposed.Memory controller: Licensed DDR4/LPDDR4 controller IP behind an SF-MEM->AXI4 bridge (bridge is a proposed MemoryFlow addition).
proposed.External memory interface: DDR4 x32 PHY hard IP (mature node); HBM only for future advanced-node variants.
